While voxel grids do have 3D positions, the claim implies a general requirement for explicit 3D locality for the method's selection, whereas the evidence highlights that the method (Lightplane) utilizes hybrid representations including triplanes which lack clearly-defined 3D positions. Furthermore, the text describes voxel grids and triplanes as 'hashed' structures in a generalized sense, noting that triplanes do not have clearly-defined 3D positions, which complicates direct lifting. Therefore, the condition of requiring 'explicit 3D spatial locality' is not fully supported because the method explicitly includes representations (triplanes) that lack this property, and the text emphasizes the lack of clearly-defined 3D positions for these hashed structures.
